claim: Diffusional kurtosis imaging (DKI) is a methodology for measuring the extent of non-Gaussian diffusion in biological tissue.
source: Diffusional kurtosis imaging (DKI) is a methodology for measuring the extent of non-Gaussian diffusion in biological tissue, which has shown great promise in clinical diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of many neurological diseases and disorders.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about DKI that is directly stated in the abstract.

claim: DKI has shown great promise in clinical diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of many neurological diseases and disorders.
source: Diffusional kurtosis imaging (DKI) is a methodology for measuring the extent of non-Gaussian diffusion in biological tissue, which has shown great promise in clinical diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of many neurological diseases and disorders.
evidence: This claim is supported by the manuscript's citation of multiple clinical applications throughout the introduction.

claim: Robust, fast, and accurate estimation of kurtosis from clinically feasible data acquisitions remains a challenge.
source: However, robust, fast, and accurate estimation of kurtosis from clinically feasible data acquisitions remains a challenge.
evidence: This is stated as a motivation for the study in the abstract.

claim: The sub-diffusion mathematical framework provides a new accurate approach for estimating mean kurtosis.
source: In this study, we first outline a new accurate approach of estimating mean kurtosis via the sub-diffusion mathematical framework.
evidence: This is one of the main contributions stated in the abstract.

claim: The sub-diffusion extension of conventional DKI overcomes the limitation on the maximum b-value of the latter.
source: Crucially, this extension of the conventional DKI overcomes the limitation on the maximum b-value of the latter.
evidence: This is stated as a key advantage of the proposed method in the abstract.

claim: Kurtosis and diffusivity can be computed as functions of the sub-diffusion model parameters.
source: Kurtosis and diffusivity can now be simply computed as functions of the sub-diffusion model parameters.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated mathematically in Equations 8 and 9.

claim: A new fast and robust fitting procedure is proposed to estimate the sub-diffusion model parameters using two diffusion times without increasing acquisition time.
source: Second, we propose a new fast and robust fitting procedure to estimate the sub-diffusion model parameters using two diffusion times without increasing acquisition time as for the conventional DKI.
evidence: This is stated as a contribution in the abstract and demonstrated through simulations and real data analysis.

claim: The sub-diffusion-based kurtosis mapping method was evaluated using both simulations and the Connectome 1.0 human brain data.
source: Third, our sub-diffusion-based kurtosis mapping method is evaluated using both simulations and the Connectome 1.0 human brain data.
evidence: This describes the validation approach used in the study.

claim: Exquisite tissue contrast is achieved even when the diffusion encoded data is collected in only minutes.
source: Exquisite tissue contrast is achieved even when the diffusion encoded data is collected in only minutes.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and supported by the results in Figures 6 and 9.

claim: Robust, fast, and accurate estimation of mean kurtosis can be realised within a clinically feasible diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data acquisition time.
source: In summary, our findings suggest robust, fast, and accurate estimation of mean kurtosis can be realised within a clinically feasible diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data acquisition time.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by the results throughout the manuscript.

claim: DW-MRI over a period of more than 30 years has become synonymous with tissue microstructure imaging.
source: Diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DW-MRI) over a period of more than 30 years has become synonymous with tissue microstructure imaging.
evidence: This is a historical statement about the field.

claim: Measures of how water diffuses in heterogeneous tissues allow indirect interpretation of changes in tissue microstructure.
source: Measures of how water diffuses in heterogeneous tissues allow indirect interpretation of changes in tissue microstructure (Le Bihan and Johansen-Berg, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Le Bihan and Johansen-Berg, 2012.

claim: DW-MRI has predominantly been applied in the brain, where properties of white matter connections between brain regions are often studied.
source: DW-MRI has predominantly been applied in the brain, where properties of white matter connections between brain regions are often studied (Lebel et al., 2019), in addition to mapping tissue microstructural properties (Tournier, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lebel et al., 2019 and Tournier, 2019.

claim: Applications of DW-MRI outside of the brain have clinical importance and interest is growing rapidly.
source: Applications outside of the brain have clinical importance as well, and interest is growing rapidly.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to various clinical applications.

claim: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) can be performed using a single diffusion weighting (b-shell) and at least six diffusion encoding directions.
source: Whilst diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) can be performed using a single diffusion weighting, a so-called b-shell, and at least six diffusion encoding directions (Le Bihan et al., 2001), other models tend to require multiple b-shells each having multiple diffusion encoding directions.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Le Bihan et al., 2001.

claim: DKI is a primary example of a multiple b-shell, multiple diffusion encoding direction method.
source: Diffusional kurtosis imaging (DKI) is a primary example of a multiple b-shell, multiple diffusion encoding direction method (Jensen et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jensen et al., 2005.

claim: DKI is considered as an extension of DTI.
source: DKI is considered as an extension of DTI (Jensen and Helpern, 2010; Hansen et al., 2013; Veraart et al., 2011b), where the diffusion process is assumed to deviate away from standard Brownian motion, and the extent of such deviation is measured via the kurtosis metric.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jensen and Helpern, 2010; Hansen et al., 2013; Veraart et al., 2011b.

claim: In DKI, the diffusion process is assumed to deviate away from standard Brownian motion, and the extent of such deviation is measured via the kurtosis metric.
source: DKI is considered as an extension of DTI (Jensen and Helpern, 2010; Hansen et al., 2013; Veraart et al., 2011b), where the diffusion process is assumed to deviate away from standard Brownian motion, and the extent of such deviation is measured via the kurtosis metric.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about DKI supported by citations.

claim: Recent clinical benefits of using kurtosis metrics over other DW-MRI-derived measures have been demonstrated for grading hepatocellular carcinoma.
source: Recent clinical benefits of using kurtosis metrics over other DW-MRI-derived measures have been demonstrated for grading hepatocellular carcinoma (Li et al., 2022b)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2022b.

source: differentiating parotid gland tumours (Huang et al., 2022)

claim: Kurtosis metrics have been demonstrated for aiding management of patients with depression.

source: delineating acute infarcts with prognostic value (Hu et al., 2022)

claim: The routine use of DKI in the clinic has lagged due to the inability to robustly estimate the kurtosis metric.
source: The routine use of DKI in the clinic has nonetheless lagged due the inability to robustly estimate the kurtosis metric (Veraart et al., 2011a; Tabesh et al., 2011; Kuder et al., 2012; Henriques et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Veraart et al., 2011a; Tabesh et al., 2011; Kuder et al., 2012; Henriques et al., 2021.

claim: The optimal maximum b-value for DKI is dependent on tissue type.
source: with the optimal maximum b-value found to be dependent on tissue type (Poot et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Poot et al., 2010.

claim: The traditional kurtosis model is less accurate at representing the diffusion signal at large b-values.
source: This suggests that the traditional kurtosis model is less accurate at representing the diffusion signal at large b-values.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the b-value limitation mentioned in the previous sentence.

claim: Multiple b-shell, multiple direction high-quality DW-MRI data can take many minutes to acquire.
source: Moreover, multiple b-shell, multiple direction high-quality DW-MRI data can take many minutes to acquire, which poses challenges for clinical imaging protocols involving a multitude of MRI contrasts already taking tens of minutes to execute.
evidence: This is stated as a practical challenge for clinical implementation.

claim: Reduction of DKI data acquisition times through parallel imaging, optimisation of b-shells and directions have been investigated.
source: Reduction of DKI data acquisition times through parallel imaging, optimisation of b-shells and directions have been investigated (Zong et al., 2021; Heidemann et al., 2010; Zelinski et al., 2008)

claim: For DKI to become a routine clinical tool, DW-MRI data acquisition needs to be fast and provides a robust estimation of kurtosis.
source: For DKI to become a routine clinical tool, DW-MRI data acquisition needs to be fast and provides a robust estimation of kurtosis.

claim: Powder averaging over diffusion directions improves the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the DW-MRI data used for parameter estimation.

source: Whilst this approach loses out on directionality of the kurtosis, it nonetheless provides a robust method of estimating mean kurtosis (Henriques et al., 2021), a metric of significant clinical value.

claim: Mean kurtosis is a metric of significant clinical value.

claim: The sub-diffusion framework provides new, unexplored opportunities for fast and robust kurtosis mapping.

claim: The most pronounced decline of CV occurs when increasing from one to two diffusion times.
